name: Diffusion model
summary: A model that learns to turn noise into an image step by step, and makes a new image from a text prompt.
how: Start from pure noise and remove it over 20 to 50 steps.
Steer the result with a text prompt and a guidance scale of 5 to 10.
Expect smooth skin, even light and a glossy, over-detailed finish when the prompt gives no flaw.
Add a concrete flaw to the prompt, such as grain, a lens fault or a cluttered ground, to break the sheen.

origin.note: Jascha Sohl-Dickstein and co-authors publish the first diffusion method for images; it is a paper in machine learning.

adoptions.via: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain and Pieter Abbeel publish Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models.
Midjourney and DALL-E 2 put text-to-image models in the hands of illustrators and designers.
Stable Diffusion releases its weights in August, and its glossy default look spreads as a recognisable image style.

sources.title: Sohl-Dickstein et al., Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics (ICML 2015)
Ho, Jain and Abbeel, Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (2020)
